findings.description: Respawning a session launched before this PR (on a machine with codegraph) replays its old compiled context.md, which still carries the `## Code graph` paragraph telling the window to use codegraph_explore BEFORE reading files — but the respawned window no longer gets --mcp-config, so that tool is not connected. ADR 0186's 'Not migrated' list doesn't mention this; either strip the section at read time or note it there.

The intro still lists "MCP config" among the profile compiler's outputs, but this PR stopped compiling mcp.json; the same stale claim sits in docs/01-architecture.md:44 (behaviour-surface list owned by the profile compiler). Drop "MCP config" from both lists.

JSDoc on the gate's private checkout says "Detached like the conductor's checkout (decision 51)", but this PR removes the conductor's checkout and supersedes decision 51; drop the clause (decision 81 already covers the gate checkout).

process_issues.description: Skipped review-context (no CORS/HTTP/docker/CI surface; the --mcp-config removal was covered by correctness and security), review-simplicity (the diff only adds an ADR, no code construct), review-spec (no spec source), review-workflow-safety (no workflow change), review-maintainability (off default roster). Security ran single-instance despite the size gate because the diff is ~95% deletions with a small trust-boundary surface. Dropped the conventions nit on the orphaned test helpers stubCodegraph/commandScopeConfig: ADR 0186 explicitly defers them (declared out of scope).
`gh pr diff 337 -- docs/adr` was refused (gh pr diff takes no path filter); the reviewer fell back to Read/Grep on the post-change tree.
